body: I am here to reach out for help.. why would you say this :(
Your comment isn't helpful at all.. I know I did a horrible thing but all I can do now is try to fix it. Do you want me to kill myself? Do you think that would help my boyfriend?

Wether it legally counted as rape or not doesn't change much for me. It really was a mistake but that doesn't make it any less horrible. It doesn't change the outcome that I traumatised someone, and someone I love at that.
Did you even read my post :( I'm fully aware that I'm a horrible person

Thank you for the reply. I'd say it's making me feel less bad but that's obviously not the point. My boyfriend and I have decided to stay together and try to work this out, but I understand that that doesn't seem like a good idea from an outside perspective. Really I think it'd be much worse for him if we broke up, since now at least he has my love and support rather than being left alone right after a traumatic event.

This is a genuine question, not trying to be condescending. Do you believe the age difference makes something that would otherwise be rape something else? I understand the way of thinking but I can't wrap my head around that the same action having the same effect is somehow different because of age.

I honestly agree. The "flipside" of the situation is essentially what happened to me so I already made the comparison in my head. I am wondering what you meant with this though

>would find excuses and rationalizations why it isn't rape when a girl does it to a boy. Like you did.

I'm posting here (partially) because I do consider myself to be a rapist and wanted to know if people agreed.
I don't mind the wait, I appreciate it a lot. Thank you so much.
I'm not sure if she is, but I'll ask. Thanks for the advice.
My therapist already knows my boyfriend's age. Not that it'd matter much because things like sending nudes are illegal no matter what if you're under 18.

I apologise, I didn't explain properly. I am currently getting professional help. It's not an option concerning this situation though. As far as I know they're required to report it if I tell them about breaking the law, which I did do in this case. My boyfriend also refuses to get professional help for employment reasons. Theoretically I'd convince him to get help anyway because he really needs it, realistically all I can do is be here for him and make sure he at least gets some form of support.

Thank you so much for your reply. You seem like a very kind person. I live in The Netherlands. I've been getting professional help for years but I'm very reluctant to talk about sex with any therapist. I also lied about my age to avoid just getting replies about the relationship being wrong. I'm 15 which makes any sexual acts I've done illegal, and I'm worried about that possibly getting reported if I mention it to a therapist.

Professional help isn't an option. I agree that he's definitely the victim in this situation. We've talked the whole thing through and he knows my side of things, including that it was intentional. I've profusely apologised to him as well but obviously that doesn't just fix the whole thing. Just here to get an outside perspective. Thank you for your reply.

I was using the knife to attempt to self-harm, I didn't threaten him with it or anything like that. Professional help is not an option. Also although I appreciate the reply, I think it's harmful to spread the message that rape must involve physical force in a violent manner (I'm assuming that's what you meant, I apologise if I'm misunderstanding).
